aboutH2: Transforming Tides Counselling: outpatient counselling in Truro, Nova Scotia
intro: Transforming Tides Counselling is a private outpatient counselling practice in Truro, Nova Scotia. It is not a residential rehab. You come in for sessions at the office in Suite 305 of 35 Commercial Street, or meet your therapist online from anywhere in Atlantic Canada, and you go home afterwards. There are no beds, no detox and no medical care.

Addiction is one of the practice's six specialty areas, alongside anxiety, depression, grief, couples therapy and neurodiversity. The team includes a registered psychologist, Dr. Nicole Callan, plus counselling therapists, a clinical social worker, a neurofeedback practitioner and a registered dietitian. The practice advertises no waitlist and evening and weekend appointments.

pillars.title: Counselling for drinking and drug use
pillars.body: The practice's addiction page is written for people who drink more than they used to, hide it from the people around them or keep trying to quit on their own. Sessions work on facing stress without numbing it, talking honestly with loved ones and handling strong emotions. Dr. Nicole Callan, Michelle Smith, Tish Lewis and Irene Gunn all list addiction or addiction recovery among their areas of focus. This is weekly outpatient counselling, so it suits people who are safe to stay at home, or people coming back to Colchester County after a residential program.

pillars.title: Assessments, neurofeedback and nutrition
pillars.body: Through its Neurodiversity and Anxiety Therapy Program, Transforming Tides pairs counselling with other services in the same office. Adults can book an assessment for ADHD or autism. Amber Brewer runs neurofeedback brain training in person, and lists addiction, compulsive behaviour, anxiety and sleep among her areas of focus. Registered dietitian Evelena Beaton covers nutrition for mental health, binge eating and ARFID.

pillars.title: A small team that grew out of one counsellor
pillars.body: Irene Gunn, a clinical social worker, started the practice in 2018 with virtual sessions for individuals and couples, because she saw how long people were waiting in the public system. In-person sessions in Truro followed, and in 2023 the practice grew into a clinic with several disciplines. Most clinicians see teens from 16 and adults, and Grace Han offers counselling in Korean as well as English.

overview: The office is on the third floor of the 35 Commercial Street building in downtown Truro, and it is open by appointment only. People from Halifax, New Glasgow, Amherst and the rest of the province can also book online sessions, as can clients in New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland and Labrador.

There is no set program or group schedule. You choose a therapist, have a free call of about 20 minutes, and then meet one-on-one or as a couple. The practice describes three steps: getting to know you and your goals, building a plan that fits, and supporting you as you work toward it.
serviceCaption: 11 services · as described on the practice's website
afterOverview: Know the limits before you book. Transforming Tides does not offer detox, medication, residential care or crisis services, and it does not publish its fees. For someone who needs supervised withdrawal or a structured addiction program, it works best as the counselling that comes alongside or after that care, closer to home in Colchester County or online.

faqIntro: Answers come from the practice's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Transforming Tides Counselling a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. Transforming Tides Counselling is an outpatient counselling practice in Truro, Nova Scotia. You book sessions in person at 35 Commercial Street or online and go home afterwards. There are no beds, no detox and no medical care, so anyone who needs withdrawal management or live-in treatment should look at Nova Scotia Health services or a residential centre first.

faqs.q: Does Transforming Tides help with addiction?
faqs.a: Yes, through one-on-one counselling. Addiction therapy is one of the practice's six specialty areas, and several clinicians, including psychologist Dr. Nicole Callan and counselling therapists Michelle Smith and Tish Lewis, list addiction among their areas of focus. Sessions work on coping with stress without substances, talking openly with family and managing strong emotions.

Transforming Tides does not publish its fees on its website, and its recovery.com profile lists private pay. Ask during the free consultation call what your sessions will cost. Many workplace benefit plans cover registered psychologists, social workers and counselling therapists, so check your plan for the credential of the therapist you choose.

No. The practice advertises no waitlist, and most of its therapists were listed as accepting new clients in October 2026. Owner Irene Gunn has limited availability. You can pick any therapist on the online calendar and book a free consultation call at a time that suits you.

faqs.q: What happens on the free consultation call?
faqs.a: The first step is a free phone call of about 20 minutes with the therapist you choose. You briefly share what you want to work on and get a sense of what therapy with them would be like. If it feels right, you book sessions, and the therapist builds a plan with you around your goals.

Yes. Sessions are offered online across Atlantic Canada as well as in person in Truro. Some clinicians, such as Grace Han and Tish Lewis, work only virtually, while Dr. Nicole Callan, Michelle Smith, Mary Robertson and Irene Gunn offer both. Neurofeedback with Amber Brewer is in person only.

faqs.q: Where is the office, and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The office is in Suite 305 at 35 Commercial Street in downtown Truro, open by appointment only. Truro is about an hour north of Halifax on Highway 102, around 45 minutes from New Glasgow and about an hour from Amherst. Many clients from farther away use online sessions instead.

faqs.q: Does the practice see teens and couples?
faqs.a: Yes. Most therapists see teens from 16, and Mary Robertson and Tish Lewis also work with younger adolescents. Neurofeedback is available from age 8. Couples counselling is a core service, with Irene Gunn and Tish Lewis listing relationship and couples work among their focus areas.

Neurofeedback is brain-wave training offered in person by Amber Brewer, the practice's neurofeedback practitioner. An assessment measures brain-wave activity, and training sessions then work on the areas that need it. The practice describes it as a medication-free option for ADHD, anxiety, trauma, sleep and focus, and Amber Brewer lists addiction and compulsive behaviour among her areas of focus.

faqs.q: Are evening or weekend appointments available?
faqs.a: Yes. Transforming Tides advertises evening and weekend appointments. Availability depends on the clinician: Dr. Nicole Callan sees clients weekdays, evenings and some Saturdays, and several counselling therapists offer weekday and evening times. Booking is done online.
